_comment: Broadcom Wi-Fi PCI-id -> recommended driver package map for `lindos-drivers autodetect`.
Broadcom PCI vendor id is 14e4; only the wireless network-controller class (0280) is matched
here (14e4 also ships wired NICs via the in-kernel tg3 driver, which need no extra package).
Each chip lists `recommended` packages in preference order; the installer picks the first one
that apt actually offers on this system. `bcmwl-kernel-source` is the Ubuntu/Mint name for the
Broadcom STA (wl) DKMS driver; `broadcom-sta-dkms` is the Debian name for the same driver;
`firmware-b43-installer` drives the open b43 kernel driver and downloads Broadcom's firmware;
`firmware-b43legacy-installer` covers the oldest BCM4306/4301-class parts. These are proprietary
or firmware-bearing packages: lindos NEVER installs them silently — only after first-boot/OOBE

wl.note: Broadcom STA (wl) proprietary DKMS driver; conflicts with the open b43 driver.

wl-or-b43.note: STA (wl) preferred; the open b43 driver (firmware-b43-installer) is the fallback.

b43.note: Open b43 kernel driver; firmware-b43-installer downloads the redistributable firmware.

b43legacy.note: Oldest BCM4306/4301-class parts use the b43legacy driver.

default.name: unknown Broadcom wireless chip
default.note: Unrecognised Broadcom wireless device: the STA (wl) driver covers most; if it fails, install the open b43 driver (firmware-b43-installer). Check `lspci -nn` and report the id.
